## P3: a stronger source representation replaces the failed mixed-accuracy shortcut

The main theorem transfers an acquired FULL coarse-path conditional law at explicit rational inflated rates into the exact continuum endpoint law. The pathwise quadrature defect is bounded by local strengths times jump counts. A computable acceptance factor cancels both that defect and the rate inflation. Entrywise kernel domination yields acceptance at least e^-1 uniformly over supported endpoint prefixes and nonnegative filters. Tiny flip rates are handled by parity-conditioned count sampling, not rejection until a rare odd event occurs. The squared kernel uses two half-paths; incorrect extra Poisson normalization would change the law.

This genuinely removes the old physical-grid refinement factor from the receiver’s accuracy dependence, conditional on the stated source costs. The preserved contraction law survives larger rates and a sufficiently long fixed cycle; this was separately checked by the frontier worker. However, new centers, guides, projector and complete paths at the changed proposal law must be acquired. A previously validated endpoint oracle or old guide table does not supply them. The mixed-accuracy worker accepts the transfer while qualifying the full P polylog(P/delta) batch claim. The global retained-mode source at inflated rates was not executed. Fixed retained dimension, physical bounds and controlled fluctuation/acceptance costs remain explicit; no general signed-Ising polynomial runtime is proved.

The three-spin execution acquired an exponential eight-state table. At M=29 a prefix of probability about5.82e-13 had acceptance about0.928; all endpoint acceptance bounds were enclosed. The M=2 stress test is outside the uniform grid prescription and has a separate selected-prefix certificate. It distinguishes the biased proposal0.94179 from the corrected continuum value0.97854. A finite-word cumulative-error count was corrected without resampling, leaving both confidence lower bounds above95%. These are reported interval/execution results, not coordinator replay. Direct interval computation wins the fixture. The public record states a program hash, but its bytes were not acquired or hash-verified here.
